chunks: From him, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who deliberately broke his fast for one day in the month of Ramadan. He said: 'Upon him is fifteen sa's for each poor person, a mud, like what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did.'

key_terms.مُدٌّ: mud (a smaller unit of volume measurement)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation (fidya) for deliberately breaking a fast in Ramadan according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* specifies the fidya for deliberately breaking a Ramadan fast as feeding fifteen poor people, with each receiving one mud of food, mirroring the practice of the Prophet Muhammad. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is often discussed in the context of whether the expiation is an alternative to or in addition to making up the day, reflecting the scholarly emphasis on the Prophet's precedent as a primary source of legal derivation.
